entry.evidence: To better constrain CaCO3 recrystallization rates and fluid movements within sediment that may be affected by hydrothermal fluid flow

steps.action: Posed the aim of constraining CaCO3 recrystallization rates and fluid movement in sediments possibly affected by hydrothermal flow, using Ca isotopes of all eight IODP Exp. 320/321 cores.
steps.quote: To better constrain CaCO3 recrystallization rates and fluid movements within sediment

steps.action: Took up the published hypothesis of hydrothermally driven fluid flow through the oceanic crust (siphon concept) as the framing expectation.
steps.quote: Recently, the hypothesis of hydrothermally driven fluid flow through the oceanic crust has been developed

steps.action: Used published 87Sr/86Sr pore water profiles of Sites U1334–U1338 (Voigt et al.) showing a return to seawater-like values near the basement.
steps.quote: This observation supports the hypothesis of a recent fluid flux of seawater through the basement

steps.action: Measured δ44/40Ca of pore water, bulk sediment carbonate, basalt and basalt carbonate cement by double-spike TIMS, plus pore water 87Sr/86Sr for U1331–U1333, and described the site-specific depth profiles.
steps.quote: The individual sites show different patterns in their pore water depth profile.

steps.action: Checked the TIMS measurements against an IAPSO seawater standard (and NBS987 for Sr) that matched literature values.
steps.quote: Ten measurements of an IAPSO (seawater) standard yielded a δ44/40Ca value of 1.84 (± 0.03 2 SE)

steps.action: Established that the bulge-shaped pore water δ44/40Ca pattern recurs across sites, matches Sr isotope, Li+ and Sr2+ trends, and scales with crustal age and sediment thickness.
steps.quote: The extent of these bulges is negatively related to the age of the underlying oceanic crust and positively related to sediment thickness.

steps.action: Proposed that the lower-section return to seawater-like δ44/40Ca and 87Sr/86Sr reflects input of seawater-like fluid from the basement.
steps.quote: This is consistent with a scenario where an input of a seawater-like fluid from the basement takes place.

steps.action: Compared bulk carbonate δ44/40Ca with published reconstructions of the ancient seawater curve to show the sediment carries primary signals, so the pore water increase must come from crustal fluid.
steps.quote: The δ44/40Ca of the bulk carbonate sediments agrees overall with reconstructions of ancient δ44/40Ca of the seawater

steps.action: Inferred the precipitation ages of intra-basalt carbonate cements from their 87Sr/86Sr against the seawater curve (Fig. 6).
steps.quote: indicating a similar age of carbonate formation (16–21 Ma), however, offset by 30 and 34 Myr to the crust formation

steps.action: For Site U1337, proposed lateral diffusive flow above the chert layer as a rival to the published interpretation of diffusive exchange with the ocean.
steps.quote: However, a lateral diffusive flow is more capable to explain these observations

steps.action: Rejected a recrystallization-only explanation for the high δ44/40Ca in upper U1337, since it would require implausibly low rates, and favoured modern seawater input supported by high 87Sr/86Sr.
steps.quote: This observation rather suggests that the δ44/40Capw is elevated by modern seawater input

steps.action: Stated two rival conceptual models: a temporal evolution of fluid flux along the age transect versus site-specific sediment properties and location as the controls.
steps.quote: Two conceptual models may explain the differences between Sites U1331 and U1338.

steps.action: Designed the test of the two hypotheses as modelling recrystallization and fluid flow rates of each core from pore water and leachate δ44/40Ca.
steps.quote: To test the hypotheses, we used the δ44/40Ca of the pore water and CaCO3 leachates to model carbonate recrystallization and fluid flow rates

steps.action: Adapted the Richter and DePaolo / Fantle and DePaolo diagenesis model with an advection term, depth-variable M, and a second-order Runge–Kutta scheme in Fortran and Python.
steps.quote: carbonate recrystallization and fluid flow rates were determined using the model of Richter and DePaolo (39) and Fantle and DePaolo (11)

steps.action: Excluded the zero-advection model (v = 0) for most sites because it could not reproduce the profiles.
steps.quote: most of the sites of this study require

steps.action: Set the model conditions: fluid flow starting 500 kyr after crust formation and four flux scenarios of increasing complexity (zero, constant, linear, time-dependent).
steps.quote: We test four different fluid-flux models, with increasing complexity

steps.action: Fitted the model to each site's profiles to estimate time-dependent initial recrystallization rates and maximum fluid velocities (Table 2, Fig. 8, Fig. 9).
steps.quote: The time-dependent initial carbonate recrystallization rates of the presented sites have been determined by best fit

steps.action: Compared the four flux scenarios against the measured data and found that the time-dependent velocity model fits best.
steps.quote: provides the best fit for the measured data

steps.action: Compared modelled fluxes with Li+, Sr2+ and Sr isotope profiles, which indicate higher fluxes at U1331–U1333 and upper U1337 than modelled.
steps.quote: indicating a higher fluid flux than modeled

steps.action: Kept the low-flux model by arguing that high flux would have overprinted the turbidite and double bulges, and attributed the misfit to a model limitation with alternating carbonate content and to lateral flow.
steps.quote: the model may not reproduce sites with alternating carbonate content accurately

steps.action: Rejected the temporal evolution hypothesis because U1333 has the lowest maximum velocity and a higher recrystallization rate than the younger U1334.
steps.quote: contradicting the hypotheses of the time evolution series of the fluid flux of the Sites of IODP Exp. 320/321 transect

steps.action: Compared the U1338 rate with Voigt et al.'s Sr-derived rates and reran the Ca model with their fixed M value, which gave an even lower R.
steps.quote: A calculation with the fixed M value used by Voigt et al. (51) in our Ca model leads to even lower R value

steps.action: Refined the account: rates co-vary with sediment thickness and CaCO3 content (lithology control) and plausibly with distance to seamounts and topography.
steps.quote: suggesting that the carbonate recrystallization and fluid velocity are controlled by the lithology

steps.action: Kept the hypothesis that recrystallization and fluid flux depend on site location and sediment composition as the more plausible one.
steps.quote: the hypothesis that carbonate recrystallization and fluid flux depend on the sites’ location and sediment composition is more plausible

Conditions found: existing IODP cores along a crustal age transect

tree.answer: Nature repeats the setting at eight sites of different age, thickness and lithology
Partly: four flux scenarios and a fixed-M rerun were tested, but tracer data at U1331–U1333 disagree with the modelled low flux
Location and sediment composition hypothesis judged more plausible; temporal evolution contradicted by U1333

end.claim: Carbonate recrystallization rates (about 0.000013e(−t/15.5) to 0.00038e(−t/100.5)) and basement-derived fluid flow (0.42–19 m/Myr) at IODP Exp. 320/321 sites depend on site location and sediment composition rather than on a temporal evolution along the crustal age transect.

decisive_move.sentence: Fitting the advection-extended recrystallization model, with four fluid-flux scenarios, to each site's δ44/40Ca profiles produced the site rates whose ordering (U1333 vs U1334) refuted the temporal evolution hypothesis.

gates.evidence: Samples came from the 2008 expedition, collected for a Cenozoic productivity record; the authors chose to measure Ca isotopes (and Sr for U1331–U1333) in view of the cited hydrothermal flow hypothesis (§1 ¶8), but the two rival models were formulated after the data were described (§4 ¶7). The temporal evolution rival could fail on the site ordering of model rates and did (§4.3 ¶4). The kept claim is judged 'more plausible' and was not set against a test it could fail; model-tracer mismatches were absorbed (§4.3 ¶3–¶4). No fit criterion or hypothesis was fixed in advance.

imports.item: Second-order strong-stability-preserving Runge–Kutta time stepping (Gottlieb et al. 2001)
Continuity equation (conservation law) for the advective fluid velocity term
Isotopic mass dependence of cation diffusion coefficients in water (Bourg et al. 2010), α_diff = 0.99956

novelty_claims.quote: Strontium isotope data of the pore water were analyzed for Sites U1331, U1332, and U1333, as those data were not available in the literature
[...] a time-depending change of the fluid velocity rate into a carbonate recrystallization model
instead of the Euler approach used in previous models

limits: Sub-claims: the site rates are presented as best fits (estimate_with_resolution in form), but no uncertainties, misfit statistics, or parameter-trade-off analysis are reported, so the resolution is not shown. Sites U1336 and U1337 were not modelled (§4.2 ¶7); the U1337 lateral-flow interpretation is best_explanation from tracers alone. The modelled low fluxes at U1331–U1333 conflict with tracer evidence for high fluxes (§4.3 ¶3); this is resolved by argument, not by a further test. The paper reports rate values inconsistently: §4.2 ¶6 gives 0.0038e−t/100.5 against 0.00038 in the abstract and Table 2, and §4.3 ¶6 gives U1335 as 0.00033e(−t/100.5) against 0.000033e(−t/100) in Table 2. The supplements (model equations 7–10, data tables) were not supplied, so fitting procedures cannot be checked. Inference: the two rival hypotheses appear to have been formulated after inspecting the profiles. The temporal evolution rival is rejected mainly on one site pair (U1333 vs U1334). No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.support: The paper argues that 87Sr/86Sr and δ44/40Ca indicate input of relatively modern seawater, better explained by lateral diffusive flow with some upward flow.
disagreements.quote: However, a lateral diffusive flow is more capable to explain these observations

disagreements.target: Fisher and Wheat 2010; Voigt et al. 2015; Villinger et al. 2017: crustal seawater interacts only with the lower part [...]
disagreements.support: The flattening of the bulges with site age is read as possible flushing of the whole sedimentary column.
disagreements.quote: Thus, the uptaken seawater may not only interact with the lower part of the [...]

disagreements.target: Richter and DePaolo (1987) model with zero fluid velocity
disagreements.support: A model run with v = 0 fails to reproduce most site profiles, so an advection term is required.
disagreements.quote: While Richter and DePaolo (39) choose 0 as value for the fluid velocity rate

disagreements.target: Voigt et al. (2015) Sr-derived recrystallization rates for Site U1338
disagreements.support: The Ca-derived rate is lower; the difference is attributed to Voigt's omission of fluid flux and use of an averaged M, and a rerun with fixed M lowers R further.
disagreements.quote: However, the model of Voigt et al. (51) does not implement a fluid flux and uses an averaged sediment property value M

disagreements.target: Fluid flux expected from low heat flow (Fisher 2004; Pälike et al. 2010)
disagreements.support: Element and isotope profiles at U1331–U1333 and upper U1337 indicate seawater-like compositions implying more flux than heat flow predicts.
disagreements.quote: higher than the possible fluid flux predicted by the low heat flux
